title: Three-colorability property
statement: Let $v$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $G$ be a graph on the vertex set $\{0,1,\ldots,v-1\}$, encoded by assigning a Boolean value to each two-element vertex set. The three-colorability property of $G$ is the Boolean value that is true exactly when the vertices of $G$ can be colored with three colors so that adjacent vertices receive different colors.
caveat: The supplied snippet does not include the definition of graph colorability or how Boolean edge values determine adjacency.
